findings.quote: | A number from the menu — "7", "run 13", "17 and 18" | §0, the item's own note (`references/items.md`) | the sections that note names, and this table's row for the ask the item performs · §1 · §10, where it writes · §0 *Every run leaves the record better organised than it found it* |
findings.problem: Old line 90 ('What the user picks fixes the operation...'), now only at references/menu.md line 21, holds the rules for an item picked by number: items 2, 3, 4, 6-11 'each take a subject the user must still name'; '**Where the user cannot name the subject an item needs, read the candidates back before starting**' (substance lines, purposes, the rows with no Sources item 1 counted); items 17-19 'take no subset' and 'narrowing item 19 and still calling it the full audit is a false claim'. In the single file this paragraph headed the §0 a bare-number run read. The new row sends a bare number (no menu printed) to items.md only, and line 14 says leave a file closed unless the table or a pointer names it; items.md does not restate these rules (item 6 says only 'One substance whose row is thin'; item 19 says nothing about narrowing). So 'run 6' with no substance can end with the run picking a thin line itself instead of reading the candidates back, and '19, just magnesium' can be run and reported as the full audit. The scenario's own examples (22, 13, 17 and 18) are unaffected: items.md carries their scope.
findings.fix: SKILL.md line 77: '| the sections that note names, and this table's row for the ask the item performs · §1 ·' -> '| the sections that note names, and this table's row for the ask the item performs · §0 What to run, and what it costs — its opening paragraphs (`references/menu.md`) · §1 ·'

findings.quote: **Where one disagrees with anything below, it governs** on the point it names, even over the rules said below to override everything else
findings.problem: In the single file 'anything below' covered every section after the opening, so a standing instruction governed whatever rule it disagreed with. Most of those rules now sit in reference files beside SKILL.md, not below this line; read literally, the clause reaches only SKILL.md's own rules. The bold lead ('which override this document') with line 14's definition of 'this document' keeps the meaning for a careful reader, so the behavioural risk is low, but the positional word no longer covers its old target.
findings.fix: '**Where one disagrees with anything below, it governs**' -> '**Where one disagrees with anything in this document, it governs**'

findings.quote: This one prints at the top of the first group because it is usually the right answer, item 22 beside it, and one clause in the block says why the numbers jump.
findings.problem: 'the block' (and 'the first group') meant the menu block earlier in the same §0; the block is now in references/menu.md and items.md has none. Informational only - no run acts on it - but it is a positional reference that now crosses a file, and a reviser reading items.md cannot resolve it from that file.
findings.fix: 'one clause in the block says why the numbers jump' -> 'one clause in the menu block (`references/menu.md`) says why the numbers jump'

findings.quote: It holds the opening above, the table under *What you are probably being asked* and the rules that follow it, §0's upkeep, §1 and §11; every other section is in a reference file beside this one
findings.problem: *Revising these rules* (old 1666-1670) is in SKILL.md (heading at line 213; the table of files at line 18 lists it there), yet line 14 lists SKILL.md's contents without it and then says every other section is in a reference file - an 'every' the files contradict, in the first text a reviser reads.
findings.fix: '§0's upkeep, §1 and §11; every other section' -> '§0's upkeep, §1, §11 and *Revising these rules*; every other section'
